findings.label: Suppliers with Current Red Flags
findings.detail: 1 current suppliers have Companies House compliance issues (historical payments were made before breaches started)

findings.label: Likely Duplicate Payments
findings.detail: 77 high-confidence duplicate groups with same supplier, amount, date and reference (3+ copies) (after filtering 71619 CSV republication artifacts)
findings.context_note: Quarterly CSV overlaps (same transaction appearing in 2 files) have been filtered out. Remaining duplicates show 3+ identical copies, which are more likely genuine overpayments.

findings.label: Suspected Split Payments
findings.detail: 2138 instances of 3+ payments just below approval thresholds in the same week
findings.context_note: Split payment detection has a high false-positive rate. Batch processing, staged invoices, and legitimate recurring payments can all trigger this pattern. FOI request for procurement approval chain recommended before drawing conclusions.

findings.label: Round-Number Payments (>£5K)
findings.detail: 3403 exact round-number payments over £5,000 — may indicate estimates rather than invoiced amounts

findings.label: Year-End Spending Pattern
findings.detail: Planning and Development spent 2.6x their monthly average in March (£879.6K above normal). Note: UK councils operate on April–March fiscal years, so elevated March spending is common as departments finalise annual budgets. Spikes above 3x warrant further scrutiny.
findings.context_note: March spending above the monthly average is expected for UK councils on April–March fiscal years. Compare against prior years' March figures for meaningful analysis.

findings.label: Rapid Payment Suppliers
findings.detail: 15 suppliers receive payments every <14 days on average. Top: "[Redacted]" (3.6 day avg, 65 payments, £114.0K)

findings.label: Benford's Law Anomaly
findings.detail: Significant deviation from Benford's Law (p < 0.001). Digit 1 deviates 11.5% from expected distribution across 700,243 transactions. Note: with 700,243 transactions, chi-squared tests are highly sensitive — the 11.5% max digit deviation is the more practical measure of anomaly.
findings.context_note: Chi-squared values on samples of 700,243+ transactions are naturally inflated and will almost always show statistical significance. The max digit deviation (11.5%) is a more meaningful indicator — deviations under 5% are typical for legitimate council spending.

findings.label: Second-Digit Benford's Anomaly
findings.detail: Second-digit distribution across 701,703 transactions shows p < 0.001 (highly significant). Digit 7 deviates 0.7% from Nigrini's expected distribution. Second-digit tests are more discriminating than first-digit for detecting round-number bias and fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Benford's second-digit analysis (Nigrini, 2012) uses chi-squared with 9 df. Critical values: 16.92 (p=0.05), 21.67 (p=0.01), 27.88 (p=0.001). n=701,703.

findings.label: Weak Competition Indicators
findings.detail: 8 contracts show signs of limited competition (short tender periods or rapid award). Top: GB-Nottingham: TPPL Nottinghamshire County Council (£1.3M)
findings.context_note: Contracts Finder does not publish bid counts. These flags use proxy signals: tender periods under 14 days and awards within 7 days of deadline. Short timelines may have legitimate explanations (framework call-offs, urgency).

key_findings.title: 10 suppliers with clock-like payment regularity
key_findings.description: These suppliers receive payments at near-identical intervals (std dev <5 days). Top: "[Redacted]" — every 3.6 days (65 payments, £114.0K)

key_findings.title: ROYAL MENCAP SOCIETY: 17223 transactions totalling £91.6M
key_findings.description: Averaging £5.3K per transaction — the council's most frequent supplier

key_findings.title: AI DOGE covers 44% of £1325.0M GOV.UK outturn
key_findings.description: Spending >£500 threshold means smaller transactions are excluded. Largest gaps: Education services, Highways and transport services, Children Social Care. This is expected — not a data quality issue.
